Context: treams-rs (Rust Ewald lattice sums). Work ONLY in the git worktree lanes/lat-inv. It holds an uncommitted test-only diff (also saved at docs-track/lattice-prop-fix.diff) that fixes two random property failures in crates/treams-core/src/properties/lattice.rs: (1) check_ewald_derivative now compares the analytic jet with the Richardson extrapolation (4 D(h) - D(2h))/3 of central differences at h=1e-5, 2e-5 instead of one central difference (the old test failed next to a diffraction threshold where the O(h^2) truncation was 6.7e-6); (2) check_tiny_normal_shift gets a conditioning term at explicit Ewald splits. First run git -C lanes/lat-inv merge --ff-only is NOT needed; the worktree is detached at 6d87dd8 (condensed into 8251007) — first update it: cd lanes/lat-inv && git stash && git checkout --detach c9beab7 && git stash pop (condensed into 8251007) (resolve if needed; the lattice files did not change between those commits, verify with git diff 6d87dd8 (condensed into 8251007) c9beab7 (condensed into 8251007) -- crates/treams-core/src/properties crates/treams-core/proptest-regressions).

New failure to investigate: a reviewer's wt.sh gates run hit properties::lattice::ewald_complete_derivative (lattice.rs ~line 173) on the unmodified integration tree: numerical derivative = -0.63-109.3i; case Cylindrical m=0, dim 1, r = [-5.8e-4, 0, 0] (approximately), k = 0.8+0.1i, eta = 0.7. The seed line was not kept. It may be the same finite-difference weakness (r very close to a lattice point, where the sum varies like log|r| or 1/r and the step h=1e-5 along the test direction is not small compared with |r|), or something else.

Tasks: a) Read the strategy of ewald_complete_derivative and reconstruct a failing case as closely as you can from these numbers (write a scratch #[test] or a proptest with a fixed case in the worktree; revert scratch tests at the end). Determine whether it fails with the ORIGINAL check (git stash to compare) and with the Richardson version. b) Use an independent high-precision reference (mpmath via .venv/bin/python or scratch: wt.sh python; scripts/generate_references.py has mpmath lattice-sum code you can reuse) to check the analytic derivative ('direction') and the sum value. Decide whether implementation or test is wrong. c) If the test is wrong: propose the minimal principled test fix (e.g. a step size scaled to the distance to the nearest lattice point / singularity, or a strategy that keeps r at least some fraction of the period away from lattice points if the documented accuracy domain in docs/validation/numerical-limits.md requires it). Do not loosen tolerances arbitrarily; derive any change from the error model. Implement it on top of the existing uncommitted diff, record a seed line for the new case in crates/treams-core/proptest-regressions/properties/lattice.txt if you obtain one (proptest prints it on failure), and verify: cd lanes/lat-inv && scratch: wt.sh rust-test --lib lattice all pass; clippy via wt.sh rust-lint clean; run ewald_complete_derivative and the other check_ewald_derivative callers with 2000 cases once (temporarily raise the case count constants in properties/mod.rs, then revert that). Save the combined diff to docs-track/lattice-prop-fix.diff (overwrite). d) If the implementation is wrong, do not change it; describe the defect precisely with numbers. Do not commit or push. Delete scratch files under lat-inv-*. Report concisely (under 600 words): reproduction, reference values and true errors, cause, fix, verification.

The test is wrong; the implementation is correct. In the reviewer's case the test's finite-difference derivative is off, not the analytic one. I fixed the test on top of the existing uncommitted diff. Nothing is committed.

Setup: the worktree lanes/lat-inv is now detached at c9beab7 (condensed into 8251007) with the old diff restored cleanly. git diff 6d87dd8 c9beab7 (condensed into 8251007) (condensed into 8251007) shows no change under properties/ or proptest-regressions/.

Reproduction. The reported case has the lower bounds of every range and y = 0 exactly, which suggests proptest shrank to it from a different random failure. The seed line wasn't kept, so I can't tell what that original failure was. I rebuilt the case as Cylindrical m=0, dim 1, rows [[1.3,0,0]], Bloch vector 0, r = [-5.8e-4, 0, 0], k = 0.8+0.1i, eta = 0.7, using the test's own direction:

  • Analytic derivative: -0.6305904201290 - 110.2292353659636i. The reported numerical value of -109.3i corresponds to x ≈ -5.83e-4.
  • Original check (one central difference, h = 1e-5): off by 5.1e-5 against a tolerance of 2.2e-5, so it fails.
  • Richardson version alone: off by 2.1e-9 here, so it passes. It still fails nearer the lattice point: at |x| = 3e-5 it is off by 5.7e-3 against a tolerance of 4.2e-4, and at |x| = 1e-5 by 1.4 against 1.3e-3.
  • At r = 0 exactly (shrinking can reach exact zeros), the check fails for every wave and dim. The sum there excludes the image at the lattice point, and a step of ±h moves the point off it so the image comes back in.

Reference values (independent mpmath direct sum, 30 digits, Im k damps it). At x = -5.8e-4:

Quantity mpmath Rust
value 1.89620626779189563 - 3.98857222081505503i 1.89620626779189538 - 3.98857222081505336i
dS/dk -2.29039535235501238 + 0.555493663373966892i matches to ~1e-15
dS/dx 2.046184057e-4 - 1097.62038095276729i matches to ~1e-15
dS/dkpar matches to ~1e-15
dS/da matches to ~1e-15
full direction -0.630590420129016 - 110.229235365963564i -0.630590420129018 - 110.229235365963632i

At x = -1e-4 every term agrees to the same level, with direction -637.0870925237005i. So the true error of the implementation is about 1e-15 relative.

Cause. Near a lattice point the image there behaves like log ρ (cylindrical m = 0) or ρ^-p (p = l+1 for spherical, |m| for cylindrical), where ρ is the distance to the point.

  • A central difference leaves a relative error of about (p+1)(p+2)/6 · (h|dr|/ρ)². With the direction's mixed x/y step this predicts 5.1e-5 here, which is exactly what was measured.
  • Richardson extrapolation leaves (p+1)(p+2)(p+3)(p+4)/30 · (h|dr|/ρ)⁴. This predicts 2.1e-9 here, again matching.
  • The documented accuracy domain does not exclude shifts near lattice points, so the right fix is the step size, not the strategy.

Fix (in crates/treams-core/src/properties/lattice.rs):

  1. A new helper, nearest_image(sum), finds the distance from r to the nearest image in the surrounding cells. It skips an image sitting exactly at r, and puts 1D spherical lattices along z.
  2. In check_ewald_derivative, the step is now h = min(1e-5, ρ / (400|dr|)). With the error formula above, this keeps the Richardson error below 7.4e-8 of the derivative for every degree the callers use (p ≤ 13). Rounding stays near 400 eps of the derivative. The tolerance is unchanged, and the step only shrinks for ρ < 5.3e-4, so every other case runs exactly as before.
  3. When r is exactly the origin lattice point, the test now holds r fixed (dr = 0) and still checks the derivatives in k, the Bloch vector and the lattice rows.
  4. recorded_cases_keep_their_properties gets a new derivative kind with three pinned cases: x = -5.8e-4, x = -3e-5 and x = 0. Undoing the step fix makes this test fail at x = -3e-5, which I checked.

Seed line: none. A random case this close to a lattice point is far too rare to get a seed from, so the deterministic pinned cases take its place; lattice.txt only has the earlier diff's two lines.

Verification:

  • wt.sh rust-test --lib lattice: 47 passed.
  • wt.sh rust-lint: clean, exit 0, after fixing clippy's float-array comparison and needless-borrow findings.
  • ewald_complete_derivative, chain_sums_do_not_depend_on_the_split and far_off_axis_chains_keep_the_ewald_identities all pass with DEFAULT_CASES and EXPENSIVE_CASES set to 2000. That run took only about 8 s, and I didn't separately confirm the higher counts took effect. The constants in properties/mod.rs are reverted.
  • A scratch sweep over cylindrical m ∈ {0, 3, -2} and spherical (3,1) and (0,0) waves, dims 1–3, at |x| from 1.3e-3 down to 1e-12 and at 0, passes with the fix. The scratch test is removed.

The combined diff (old diff plus this fix, 163 lines) is saved to docs-track/lattice-prop-fix.diff. Scratch files under lat-inv-* are deleted.
